observations:
Torah #43 is a short, tightly-structured teaching (10 lines) organized around a single conceptual axis: da'at (knowledge/consciousness) and its two poles — holy da'at (Moshe) and klipah-da'at (Bilam) — mediated by speech/mouth as the neutral instrument. All bechina-connected concepts fall naturally into three packages already proposed in torah_43_packages.json.

The three-package structure (good da'at / evil da'at / neutral peh-dibur) is comprehensive and exhausts the bechina content of the teaching:

(1) Package 1 — דַּעַת דִּקְדֻשָּׁה וּמֹשֶׁה: covers the holy da'at cluster including Moshe, holy da'at itself, and its relational form (zivug dikdushah). This is a coherent thematic family.

(2) Package 2 — דַּעַת דִּקְלִפָּה וּבִלְעָם: covers the klipah-da'at cluster including Bilam, klipah-da'at itself, its ontological definition (excesses of supernal da'at), and its relational form (sinful unions). This is the evil mirror.

(3) Package 3 — דִּבּוּר וּפֶה: covers the neutral structural axiom that mouth/speech = revelation of da'at. This is a structurally distinct domain (a principle about the nature of communication and da'at, not an assertion about holiness or evil).

New Package threshold check (requires 3+ concepts with bechina language forming an INDEPENDENT domain not captured above):

Candidate examined: 'Anger / Ka'as cluster' — da'at disturbed → anger → chokhmah departs. This is entirely eitza (causal chain) in the source text. Line 7 uses 'אֲזַי יֵשׁ כַּעַס' (then there is anger) and cites 'כָּל הַכּוֹעֵס חָכְמָתוֹ מִסְתַּלֶּקֶת' — both causal formulations, not bechina. No ka'as/chokhmah bechina cluster exists. The ka'as episode of Moshe (losing da'at when angry at the soldiers returning from Midian) is narrative illustration, not bechina-language. Disqualified.

Candidate examined: 'Zivug / Marital union cluster' — the teaching opens with the statement that unions are drawn from da'at. However, zivug dikdushah is assigned to Package 1 and zivugim shel aveirah to Package 2. There is no third zivug concept that would form an independent package. The zivug nodes are faces of their respective da'at packages, not an independent domain.

Conclusion: The three packages in torah_43_packages.json fully account for all bechina-language concepts in the source text. No new package is warranted.
